long_biography.plain_text:
A magazine article about quarks changed Robert Lourie's ambitions while he was serving as a Navy radar technician. He had expected to study electrical engineering, but began teaching himself mathematics and physics instead. He took his university entrance tests aboard an aircraft carrier and won early admission to MIT.

His support for medical research included funding for specialist imaging equipment. With Ivana Stolnik-Lourie, he provided a challenge grant for a PET/CT scanner at Stony Brook University, dedicated to research in psychiatry and neurology. Lalit and Kavita Bahl met the challenge in full, helping the university acquire the scanner for its Medical and Research Translation building.
